key_insight: AEAPTMS passivation makes perovskite surfaces electronically more uniform, boosting and stabilizing the light-induced surface photovoltage while reducing grain-boundary barriers.
engineering_relevance: This suggests amino-silane passivation can improve charge-carrier landscape stability in perovskite solar cells, helping reduce photovoltage losses at the device-relevant surface.
method: Amplitude-modulated Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) on mixed-cation, mixed-halide perovskite thin films
Comparison of dark contact potential difference (CPD) and illuminated surface photovoltage (SPV) before and after AEAPTMS passivation
Wavelength-dependent SPV plus grain-boundary vs grain-interior separation to assess disorder and potential barriers
evidence_signal: Passivation narrowed dark CPD spread from about 45.7 to 14.6 mV, increased steady-state SPV from about 345 to 417 mV, and reduced the stabilisation time constant from about 840 to 470 s.
watch_item: The results are nanoscale surface measurements on thin films, so device-level performance gains and long-term operational stability still need direct confirmation.
paper_title: Understanding surface potential dynamics of passivated perovskites via Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
